videos.caption: Here's everything that happened in America in the last 12 hours. The U.S. Supreme Court blocked a Trump-backed Missouri congressional map for the midterms, ruling in an unsigned order that changing boundary lines after absentee voting had already begun would usher in absolute electoral chaos. A massive nor’easter battered the American East Coast with coastal flooding and power outages, prompting governors in New York and New Jersey to declare emergency states while forced flight delays and major festival cancellations hit the region. The Supreme Court ruled six to three to let states check voter citizenship records, temporarily staying a lower court order and allowing election officials to resume using the Department of Homeland Security's revamped federal database. Iran proposed reopening the strategic Strait of Hormuz and resuming frozen nuclear talks within seven days, offering the diplomatic compromise if the United States lifts its naval blockade and waives existing oil trade sanctions. The White House signaled it will exclude CNN from traveling on Air Force One, retaliating against the media network during a Saturday trip to Tennessee despite a recent federal judge's emergency order restoring general press credentials. Chinese President Xi Jinping concluded his high-profile United States visit without announcing any major new agreements, wrapping up discussions with President Trump that yielded only a previously negotiated two-month trade truce extension. New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Caldwell resigned abruptly following serious sexual harassment allegations, stepping down from office after Governor Sherrill publicly joined widespread state leadership demands calling for the immediate resignation. Severe immigration enforcement sweeps across Texas, Kansas, and Oklahoma sparked food supply alarms, with major meatpacking groups warning that heightened workplace crackdowns are forcing employee absences and could drastically spike consumer grocery prices. Texas police arrested a seventeen-year-old suspect following a fatal shooting near a Houston high school, launching a criminal homicide investigation after another seventeen-year-old student was found dead outside the campus grounds. #USNews #NewsUpdate #BreakingNews #newsfeed #News

(SEPTEMBER 26): President Trump has rejected Iran’s seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. “I rejected their deal. They want to make a deal where they open the strait immediately because they’re losing so badly,” Trump told reporters as he departed the White House. “You know why they’re dying? Because they have no money coming in because they get their money from the Hormuz Strait.” Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had said Friday that Tehran submitted a “concrete seven-day plan” through Qatari mediators — one he described as asking for nothing beyond what was already agreed to in June’s Memorandum of Understanding, which collapsed within days of being signed. Trump said he remains open to negotiating in general: “They want to make a deal and I think that’s fine. I’d like to make a deal, too. But that deal would not be acceptable.”
